strings.name: Mark Liu
strings.role: Former TSMC chairman, Micron director and TCIP founder
strings.summary: Born in Taiwan, Mark Liu has a background in semiconductor research and manufacturing management. He served as TSMC co-CEO and chairman, then pursued investment, corporate governance and industrial-policy work. His contribution involves teams and production organizations, not sole invention of advanced processes or company achievements.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Nationality follows TSMC’s annual report. Co-CEO and chairmanship periods, retirement announcement and actual transition, and board nominations and election results are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Contributed to TSMC technology and management, advancing semiconductor manufacturing and the global foundry industry.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Electrical engineering bachelor’s from National Taiwan University; Berkeley master’s and doctorate in electrical engineering and computer science, earned in 1980 and 1983 respectively.
strings.facts.f2.label: Work after TSMC retirement
strings.facts.f2.value: Chairs J&M Copper Beech Ventures, founded Berkeley’s TCIP Center and joined Micron’s board in 2025.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Advanced manufacturing management
strings.highlights.h1.text: Moved from research and fab management into TSMC leadership, advancing production and manufacturing capability through employees, customers and partners.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Industry and policy research
strings.highlights.h2.text: Founded the Technology Competitiveness and Industrial Policy Center; selected with C.C. Wei for SIA’s 2025 Robert N. Noyce Award.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Nominated for Micron board reelection
strings.timeline.t1.text: The company includes him among nominees for the next shareholders meeting; this is not a completed 2027 reelection.
strings.timeline.t2.title: TCIP reports his election to the NAE
strings.timeline.t2.text: The center reports his election to the 2026 class for leadership in advanced semiconductor mass production; distinct from fellow honoree H.-S. Philip Wong.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joins Micron’s board
strings.timeline.t3.text: Appointed alongside Christie Simons as a director, not as Micron CEO.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Retires from TSMC
strings.timeline.t4.text: Leaves after the shareholders meeting; C.C. Wei becomes chairman while remaining CEO, separate from the retirement intention announced in 2023.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes TSMC chairman
strings.timeline.t5.text: Moves from president and co-CEO to chairman, serving through June 2024.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes president and co-CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Moves from co-chief operating officer to co-CEO; this period is not a sole-CEO tenure.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins TSMC
strings.timeline.t7.text: Enters foundry manufacturing and company management after Intel and AT&T Bell Laboratories.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earns Berkeley doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completes a doctorate in electrical engineering and computer science and joins Intel’s process-technology work that year.
